data.title: Jensen Huang's $350 Million CoreWeave Deal Raises Questions About AI Financing
data.description:
CoreWeave (CRWV, Financials) is set to receive $350 million in computing-related spending from the charitable foundation established by former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang and his wife, Lori, according to recent tax disclosures.

The Jen-Hsun & Lori Huang Foundation's last filing revealed the promise. A June Nvidia filing named CoreWeave as the receiver and indicated $108.3 million spent.

The funding supports the Computing Initiative for Open Science, which gives researchers access to large-scale GPU computing resources.

The foundation does not directly use computing power, CoreWeave claimed. Scientific research grant awardees receive the resources.

Investors are scrutinizing AI infrastructure firms' financial interactions with consumers. For its cloud computing company, CoreWeave relies on powerful GPUs. Nvidia is a key stakeholder.

This is the Huang Foundation's greatest 2025 donation. Almost three times its 2024 donations, the organization gave $373 million last year.

At Dec. 31, 2025, its assets were $12.7 billion, up from $9.2 billion. About 90% of the assets were Nvidia shares.

The foundation gave the California College of the Arts $19 million and the Hong Kong University of Science and Technology $1.2 million.

CoreWeave investors see the pledge as more computing service demand, but it also shows how the AI infrastructure sector is financially intertwined.

Investors will scrutinize future disclosures for CoreWeave's remaining computing obligations and revenue contribution.

data.title: RAG foundation still aims to cut Evonik stake after BASF exit
data.description:
Evonik's top shareholder, the RAG foundation, said on Friday it still aims to gradually reduce its stake in the German chemicals company to 25.1%, after BASF ended its pursuit of Evonik.

  • "We regret that BASF has abandoned its efforts to acquire Evonik without any in-depth exploratory talks having taken place between the executive boards of the two companies," the foundation told Reuters in a statement.

  • BASF abandoned its pursuit of Evonik after it said its smaller rival remained unwilling to engage despite a potential further increase of its takeover offer.

  • Shares in Evonik lost 16% in a record daily drop on Thursday, closing at €18, well below BASF's most recent offer of €24.

  • As part of its efforts, BASF approached the government of North Rhine-Westphalia, where Evonik is based, and the RAG foundation, outlining commitments on plants, jobs and training, two people familiar with the matter said.

  • NRW state premier Hendrik Wuest sits on the board of trustees of the RAG foundation, which holds 43% of the group's shares. Any sale of the foundation's shares would require the board's approval.

data.title: PPG named to TIME Magazine’s ‘America’s Top Manufacturers 2027’ list
data.description:
PPG () today announced its inclusion in TIME Magazine’s America's Top Manufacturers 2027. The list recognizes the strongest 250 manufacturing companies across three categories: financial performance, innovation capacity and employment excellence. PPG ranked third in the Chemicals and Materials group and No. 43 overall.

“This recognition is a testament to the dedication and expertise of our employees around the world,” said Bryan Iams, PPG chief communications officer. “Every day, our teams develop innovative solutions, advance our manufacturing capabilities and help customers solve complex challenges. This recognition reflects our commitment to protecting and beautifying the world through sustainable innovation and operational excellence.”

America’s Top Manufacturers 2027, developed in conjunction with data analysis firm Statista, lists the top 250 companies based on a range of financial, innovation and employment metrics. These include sales and profit growth, R&D spending and patent assets, and employee productivity and turnover. The list only includes companies that had sales of more than $100 million in 2025 and have manufacturing facilities in the U.S.

PPG: WE PROTECT AND BEAUTIFY THE WORLD®

At PPG (), we work every day to develop and deliver the paints, coatings and specialty products that our customers have trusted for more than 140 years. Through dedication and creativity, we solve our customers’ biggest challenges, collaborating closely to find the right path forward. With headquarters in Pittsburgh, we operate and innovate in more than 50 countries and reported net sales of $15.9 billion in 2025. We serve customers in construction, consumer products, industrial and transportation markets and aftermarkets. To learn more, visit www.ppg.com.

data.title: Engineer of train mega-merger steps on third rail
data.description:
By Jeffrey Goldfarb

Jim Vena champions precision in railroading, but played a bit fast and loose with his controversial mega-merger. The Union Pacific CEO was caught on camera saying he might hike prices "3% to 4% extra" for customers that oppose his company’s acquisition of rival Norfolk Southern , to “teach you a lesson.” As the $85 billion deal heads into the final stage of a rigorous regulatory review, the flippant remark has the power to derail it.

Union Pacific said Vena’s comment in March was an "offhand" one and that it does not retaliate against shippers. Maybe, but like joking about a bomb on an airplane, authorities will take it seriously. Moreover, by fighting against the video’s release until a Surface Transportation Board judge ordered it earlier this month, the company gifted ammunition to deal opponents at a bad time. It puts the statement front and center just as the US political tide turns and the STB unpicks how competition will be affected by a single operator spanning more than 50,000 miles across 43 states.

The bar is already high. Railway operators are required to persuade trustbusters that a merger enhances competition, not just preserves the status quo. It’s a painstaking process. Union Pacific unveiled its proposal in July 2025 and completion isn’t expected until the second half of 2027.

Although Vena has rallied support, including from trucker Knight-Swift Transportation, boilermakers and legislators, there are shippers, unions and elected officials lined up against his transcontinental railway plan, too. A bipartisan group of senators on Wednesday urged the STB to reject the merger, arguing it would raise prices.

They also called out the deal engineer's “threat.” Rival Canadian Pacific Kansas City went so far as to use the comment as the basis for asking regulators to torpedo Union Pacific's acquisition plan. Investors have become warier of approval since the video's release, according to Breakingviews calculations.

Although indefensible, Vena’s mouthful of foot is insufficient on its own to warrant scrapping a complicated corporate marriage. The STB, comprising three Republicans and a Democrat with one vacant seat, will scrutinize competing perspectives on prices, jobs, supply chains, cost savings, market share and much more to determine whether Union Pacific will make things better for all stakeholders.

Even with the STB’s blessing, accompanying conditions may be that much more rigorous after factoring in the CEO’s choice of words. Any post-merger oversight also might be especially stringent. More than anything, though, chances are growing that Vena and his shareholders will be the ones who get taught a lesson.

Follow Jeffrey Goldfarb on X and Linkedin.

CONTEXT NEWS

Public comments on Union Pacific's proposed merger with rival railway operator Norfolk Southern were due on November 18.

An administrative law judge at the Surface Transportation Board, the regulator reviewing the deal, on November 4 ordered Union Pacific to remove a "confidential" designation and make public a video of CEO Jim Vena speaking at a Southwest Association of Rail Shippers, or SWARS, conference on March 17.

"The Board has serious concerns about whether Vena's statement at SWARS — as reflected in the recording — may be influencing certain stakeholders' willingness to participate in this proceeding or share their own views about fear of commercial repercussions," according to the order. "The Board will not tolerate actual or threatened retaliation against a stakeholder for participating in this or any other proceeding before the Board."

In the video, Vena said if the merger doesn't go through, Union Pacific would keep operating. "And if I stick around, which I probably will, I'll probably increase everybody's rates that said they didn't want a seamless railroad by 3 or 4 extra percent to teach you a lesson," he said.

Union Pacific said it doesn't retaliate against customers and characterized Vena's remark as an "offhand comment."

data.title: Danaher, Microsoft Partner on AI Platform for Scientific Instruments
data.description:
By Kelly Cloonan

Danaher and Microsoft are teaming up to develop an agentic AI platform designed for scientific instruments and laboratories.

Danaher said Friday the partnership aims to help streamline experimental operations and speed up laboratory findings.

The platform will be built on Microsoft's AI technologies using Danaher's scientific, workflow and instrumentation expertise. It will aim to enable reuse and interoperability across technologies, so specialized products can be built on a shared foundation while remaining open to agents and digital solutions in multi-vendor laboratories, Danaher said.

Danaher said that while the platform is still under development, its first commercial AI applications--including an AI assistant designed to provide product support for cellular imaging systems--will reach its customers this year. Additional agent-enabled instruments from Danaher businesses that use the platform are planned for 2027, the company said.

"With Microsoft, we are building a common foundation, so our instruments and laboratories work together consistently, as one connected Danaher," said Julie Sawyer Montgomery, Danaher's president and chief executive.

Write to Kelly Cloonan at kelly.cloonan@wsj.com

InPost is now wholly-owned by the Consortium and has delisted from Euronext Amsterdam.

A new chapter for InPost

Completion of the acquisition marks a significant milestone for InPost, a leading European out-of-home e-commerce enablement platform. The business will continue to operate as a standalone, operationally independent company under its existing brand, with its headquarters, management structure and innovation remaining in Poland. Founder Rafał Brzoska continues to lead the Company as CEO, and the executive leadership team which has underpinned InPost’s success to date remains in place, carrying forward the vision he set out when founding the business in 1999.

With an out-of-home network of over 100,000 locations, comprising more than 70,000 automated parcel lockers and close to 30,000 pick-up and drop-off points, the Consortium believes InPost has a clear path to extend its reach further. Backed by the Consortium’s capital, expertise, deep sector experience and shared vision, InPost will work to strengthen its position in Poland and expand across Europe, including in the UK, Italy, France, Spain, Portugal and the Benelux region. InPost’s home market of Poland will remain the blueprint for new innovations, which will then be scaled across InPost’s wider European network.

At its core, InPost is a technology-driven business aiming to redefine the European e-commerce sector by improving the delivery experience for consumers and merchants alike. The Consortium will accelerate investment in InPost’s digital offering and consumer experience, including its mobile app, as it innovates to increase its consumer appeal. Enabled by this technology platform and leading out-of-home network, the Consortium believes InPost is well-positioned to benefit from structural sector tailwinds, including increasing e-commerce penetration, rising consumer demand for speed and convenience, and the shift towards more sustainable delivery solutions.

To help deliver this growth, InPost and FedEx are exploring separate commercial opportunities to provide FedEx merchants access to InPost’s B2C capabilities while leveraging FedEx’s global network to support the Company’s growth. As an example, the two companies have entered into arm’s length commercial agreements enabling selected recipients the use of InPost’s last-mile capabilities and out-of-home infrastructure in Europe.

The partnership between the Consortium and InPost aims to deliver benefits for all InPost stakeholders. Employees will continue to be able to build their careers within a strengthened business, empowered by a fast-growing, innovative culture. Merchants can expect a more advanced, better-connected delivery network and continued investment in the technology that serves their consumers. And consumers across Poland and Western Europe will have the opportunity to experience greater convenience, more choice and a faster way to shop and receive goods – driven by InPost’s consumer-centric innovations and growing delivery network.

The Consortium believes its investment, collective sector knowledge and experience will support InPost in continuing to build a leading platform for parcel delivery and returns across Europe.

Rafał Brzoska, Founder and CEO of InPost, said: “This partnership delivers the long-term capital, global reach and deep technology expertise we require to build on what we have already achieved together as a leading European e-commerce enabler. I’m proud of how far we have come since founding InPost in 1999 in Poland, growing into one of Europe’s largest delivery networks. We’re taking this step with partners who have known InPost for years and understand our business and ambitions. With the Consortium’s expertise and backing, we will accelerate our investment in the technology and consumer experience that set us apart, bringing them to even more consumers and merchants across Europe.”

Ranjan Sen, Managing Partner at Advent, said: “We began our journey with InPost and Rafał in 2017, when we invested in a promising local leader with the potential to become a European champion. InPost has since grown to over 100,000 locations across Poland and Western Europe, and we are proud to reiterate our conviction in Rafał and his team. Drawing on our successful track record of investing in both InPost and the wider logistics sector, we look forward to working alongside our Consortium partners to help drive the next stage of the Company’s growth.”

Raj Subramaniam, President and CEO of FedEx, said: “FedEx is the heartbeat of the global industrial economy, and InPost has built a leading position in Europe’s out-of-home delivery segment. Connecting our global network of 3 million businesses and 225 million recipients with InPost’s last-mile capabilities gives both businesses a potential springboard for profitable growth. We see significant opportunity to expand our commercial arrangements across Europe and look forward to building on it as members of the Consortium.”

Didier Stoessel, Co-CEO of PPF, said: “When we first invested in InPost almost three years ago, we saw a strong business model with long-term growth potential as e-commerce and out-of-home delivery continue to expand across Europe. Our conviction in the Company has only strengthened since then. We are pleased to build on that relationship now by reinvesting alongside our Consortium partners and leveraging our knowledge of the Company as InPost enters this next chapter.”

Consortium structure

Following completion, the Consortium is structured with Advent holding 37%, FedEx holding 37%, A&R holding 16% and PPF holding 10%. A&R has fully rolled-over its holdings in the Company and PPF has reinvested part of the proceeds from the tender of its existing stake to become a shareholder in the Consortium.

Notes to Editors:

About InPost

InPost has revolutionised e-commerce parcel delivery in Poland and is now one of the leading out-of-home e-commerce enablement platforms in Europe. Founded in 1999 by Rafał Brzoska, InPost provides delivery services through our network of more than 70,000 Automated Parcel Machines (“APMs”) across nine European countries, alongside courier and fulfilment services for e-commerce merchants. InPost’s locker network provides consumers with a cheaper, more flexible and convenient delivery option. Powered by in-house technology, InPost continuously develops and tests new services, from digital tools to e-commerce solutions, to make buying and selling online simpler for consumers and merchants.

About Advent

Advent is a leading global private equity investor committed to working in partnership with management teams, entrepreneurs, and founders to help transform businesses. With 17 offices across five continents, we oversee more than USD $109 billion in assets under management* and have made 460 investments across 45 countries.

Since our founding in 1984, we have developed specialist market expertise across our five core sectors: business & financial services, consumer, healthcare, industrial, and technology. This approach is bolstered by our deep sub-sector knowledge, which informs every aspect of our investment strategy, from sourcing opportunities to working in partnership with management to execute value creation plans. We bring hands-on operational expertise to enhance and accelerate businesses.

As one of the largest privately-owned partnerships, our 675 colleagues leverage the full ecosystem of Advent’s global resources, including our Portfolio Support Group, insights provided by industry expert Operating Partners and Operations Advisors, as well as bespoke tools to support and guide our portfolio companies as they seek to achieve their strategic goals.

*Assets under management (AUM) as of June 30, 2026. AUM includes assets attributable to Advent advisory clients as well as employee and third-party co-investment vehicles.

About FedEx

FedEx Corp. () provides customers and businesses worldwide with a broad portfolio of transportation, ecommerce, and business services. With annual revenue of $86 billion, the company offers integrated business solutions utilizing its flexible, efficient, and intelligent global network. Consistently ranked among the world’s most admired and trusted employers, FedEx inspires its more than 450,000 employees to remain focused on safety, the highest ethical and professional standards, and the needs of their customers and communities. FedEx is committed to connecting people and possibilities around the world responsibly and resourcefully, with a goal to achieve carbon-neutral operations by 2040. To learn more, please visit fedex.com/about.

About A&R

A&R is an independent investment company founded by Rafał Brzoska that manages a diversified portfolio of private and public investments. A&R has been a shareholder in InPost since its IPO.

About PPF

PPF Group, a privately held investment holding company, operates in 25 countries across Europe, North America and Asia. It invests in telecommunications, media, financial services, real estate, ecommerce, industry, biotechnology and other sectors. PPF Group held assets worth EUR 42.1 billion and employed approximately 34,000 people worldwide (as of 30 June 2026).

data.title: CDW Canada Named an IDC CIO Awards Canada 2026 Winner
data.description:
CDW Canada, a leading provider of technology solutions and end-to-end services for Canadian organizations, has been named a 2026 International Data Corporation (IDC) CIO Awards Canada winner. CDW Canada was recognized for putting governed AI to work within its own Security Operations Centre, using its internal security team as "customer one" to demonstrate the same practices it helps customers adopt.

Canadian organizations are entering a new phase of AI adoption where success will be determined less by access to technology and more by the ability to govern, secure and operationalize it. CDW Canada’s award-winning initiative applies AI to security operations, with governance built into the workflow and experienced security professionals validating every AI output before action is taken. This initiative has reduced the time analysts spend on repetitive triage while ensuring decisions remain with human analysts.

Now it in its fifth year, the IDC CIO Awards Canada recognize Canadian organizations and IT leaders delivering measurable business value through technology.

"We hold our own AI to the same standard our customers expect: secure, governed and accountable to the people using it," said Ginette Adragna, Senior Vice President and General Manager, CDW Canada. "Being our own first customer means that when we help organizations move AI from experimentation to real business value, we're sharing what we've already learned in practice. We're honoured to be recognized by IDC."

This recognition reflects how CDW Canada helps organizations of every size create AI-ready environments. Midsize organizations face many of the same AI, governance and security pressures as large enterprises, often with fewer resources. By applying these technologies internally first, CDW Canada brings practical, real-world experience to customers as they work to adopt AI responsibly and turn their investments into measurable business outcomes.

About CDW Canada

CDW Canada Corp. is the strategic end-to-end technology partner that cuts through complexity to turn customer ambition into outcomes. Working with organizations across the business, government, education and healthcare sectors, CDW enables organizations to navigate an increasingly complex technology market and turn their technology investments into lasting value. data.title: Anthropic's $2 trln IPO may be last hurrah
data.description:
By Karen Kwok

Dario Amodei took Wall Street to Claude nine, if only briefly. Shares in Anthropic , the AI lab he runs, surged 34% on its debut Thursday, briefly valuing it at $2 trillion. But growth is slowing and profit is still uncertain. It puts the rest of the artificial intelligence trade under a cloud.

Anthropic's entrance onto public markets comes against an unsettled backdrop. The CBOE Volatility Index , Wall Street's preferred fear gauge, has hovered above 25 this week - a level that typically deters bankers from pushing new listings. Shares in chipmakers, Big Tech groups and data-center operators known as neoclouds have swooned following midterm elections that elevated a crop of AI skeptics. The dramatic departure of Nvidia's founder Jensen Huang adds more ambiguity.

Anthropic is the first large machine-learning model maker to go public. At its opening price, the enterprise is valued at 14.5 times next fiscal year's revenue forecasts from Needham and Morningstar. That is even richer than Elon Musk's SpaceX , which trades at 9 times sales for the same period, according to Visible Alpha.

The problem is that IPO buyers are paying this premium just as Anthropic's breakneck growth faces signs of deceleration. Revenue surged more than 1,200% in the first nine months of this year from a year earlier. But spending on tokens passed through the company's models rose just 3% in the week of November 15 relative to a month ago among businesses tracked by Ramp AI.

There are other reasons to doubt the durability of its economics. The falling price customers are paying per token is a sign of Anthropic's slipping pricing power. Its operating margin slipped to -3% in the third quarter from 8% in the second quarter, partly reflecting the soaring expense of energy. And Anthropic has committed some $900 billion to the chips, cloud services and data centers needed to train and run its AI models, with more than $70 billion due over the 12 months following September 2026.

Public investors will now have the opportunity to scrutinize those trade-offs every three months. The reaction in adjacent sectors suggests the market is already uneasy. Nvidia and Broadcom shares fell 1.6% on Thursday, while neocloud names CoreWeave and Nebius dropped 3.1% and 6%, respectively. Anthropic's own stock later traded below its $111.50 debut price.

Ultimately, Anthropic's ability to turn the proceeds it raised into profitable revenue depends partly on a less glamorous issue: whether data centers and chips can actually arrive on time. A stellar market debut may buy the AI industry another day of confidence, and perhaps help keep the server farm boom alive for a while. But the foundations look fragile.

Follow Karen Kwok on LinkedIn and X.

CONTEXT NEWS

Anthropic's stock began trading on November 19, opening at $111.50 per share, 34% above the $83 initial public offering price.

The Claude chatbot maker and certain selling stockholders sold 980 million shares at $83 apiece in an upsized IPO, above the marketed range of $70 and $78 each.

Shares of Anthropic traded at $97 a share at 1217 ET.

data.title: CN SAMR Fines Baidu HK RMB500,000 Over Illegal Acquisition of Part of JOYY Biz
data.description:
China's State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) announced that it recently issued an administrative penalty decision against Baidu Hong Kong for illegally implementing a business concentration in its acquisition of part of the business of JOYY Inc. . Pursuant to Articles 48 and 49 of the Anti-Monopoly Law before amendment, Baidu Hong Kong was fined RMB500,000. The target business mainly provides entertainment live-streaming services to users in China through YY Live.

The regulator said Baidu Hong Kong had the legal obligation to file the business concentration in accordance with the law, but implemented the concentration without approval after filing, violating Article 25 of the Anti-Monopoly Law before amendment and constituting illegal implementation of a business concentration. Under Article 27 of the Anti-Monopoly Law before amendment, the assessment concluded that the concentration did not have the effect of excluding or restricting competition.

If the parties disagree with the above administrative penalty decision, they may apply for an administrative reconsideration with the SAMR within 60 days from receipt of the decision, or file an administrative lawsuit with the Beijing Intellectual Property Court within six months from receipt of the decision in accordance with the law. During the administrative reconsideration or litigation period, the administrative penalty decision will not be suspended.

data.title: PayPal names Claire Bramley as chief financial officer
data.description:
Payments firm PayPal said on Friday it has named Claire Bramley as chief financial officer, succeeding Jamie Miller, as part of a broader shake-up of its senior leadership team.

The executive overhaul comes as PayPal pursues an aggressive turnaround plan to restore investor confidence, battered by intensifying competition from Apple, Google and newer fintech rivals.

Bramley joins PayPal from Xero, a global small-business platform, where she has served as CFO since April 2025.

Among other appointments, the company named American Express' Kartik Mani as president and head of consumer financial services and Venmo.

Juan Rio is set to join PayPal from Brightstar.AI as executive vice-president of AI business transformation and operations at the end of the month.
